evals.name: clean-mi-month-end
evals.prompt: Month-end. Attached is our Metrc active packages export (pulled 9/30 6pm) and the physical count our team did 9/30 after close. We're a Michigan grower + processor. Why don't these match and what do we need to do?
evals.expected_output: A reconciliation report with a jurisdiction block for Michigan, the confirmed column mapping, script-computed variances on 7 quantity-compared packages out of 12 listed (net weight -23.792 g; Gummies +12 each; Live Resin -2 each), the likely tag typo (…0011 vs …0110) raised from the script's near-match note while both rows stay open as COUNTED_NOT_IN_SYSTEM / IN_SYSTEM_NOT_COUNTED until the physical label is checked, pre-roll UoM mismatch not converted, trim package not counted, unknown preroll pack counted but not in system, likely causes with confidence, draft (not submitted) actions, no invented MI adjustment reason codes or deadlines, and a sign-off block.
assertions: Reports net weight variance of -23.792 g (or -23.8 g) consistent with the script output
Treats 1A4060300003B21000000102 as a real shortfall after unit conversion: 1 lb vs 447.9 g gives -5.692 g (SHORT_IN_COUNT), not a 446.9-unit difference and not a rounding match
Flags 1A4060300003B21000000011 / ...110 as a probable tag typo to confirm against the physical label, without closing either row or counting it as two confirmed losses before that check
Does not convert the Pre-Roll 1g 'each' vs 'g' rows; asks for per-unit weight or recount
Treats Gummies +12 over-count and the counted-not-in-system package as high priority (possible untracked product)
Does not state a specific Michigan adjustment reason code, deadline, or threshold unless cited with a source
Marks all adjustments as DRAFT / not submitted and includes a reviewer sign-off block

evals.name: erp-vs-metrc-colorado-messy
evals.prompt: can u compare our ERP on hand vs metrc? colorado medical + rec cultivation. erp export attached + metrc export. some counts are blank because we didnt get to that room
evals.expected_output: Detects that the ERP file has two candidate quantity columns (Qty and Counted) and asks which represents the count before running; handles blank counted quantity as BAD_QUANTITY / not counted rather than zero; treats Metrc packages absent from a partial count as scope gaps, not losses.
assertions: Surfaces the ambiguous quantity column (Qty vs Counted) and asks the operator which one is the count, without choosing one itself or stating any variance before they answer
Does not treat the blank count for package ...103 as zero inventory
Separates packages outside the counted scope from genuine shortfalls and does not call uncounted packages losses
Asks for or flags the as-of timestamps of both files
Notes CO license types (medical and retail) and does not import rules from another state

evals.name: missing-state-and-files
evals.prompt: Our inventory is off by like 2 pounds this month. How do we fix it in Metrc?
evals.expected_output: Asks one combined question for state, license type, the traceability export and count/ERP file with as-of times; explains briefly what it will do with them; does not give state-specific adjustment instructions or reason codes; does not suggest adjusting 2 lb before root cause is found.
assertions: Asks for state and license type in a single combined question
Asks for both source files (traceability export and count/ERP) with as-of times
Does not provide a specific Metrc adjustment reason or state deadline
Explicitly advises against adjusting to force a match before finding the cause

evals.name: regression-duplicates-blank-units-rounding
evals.prompt: Can you reconcile our Metrc export against this count sheet? Both pulled 10/31 at 5pm. We're a Michigan grower. Some people double-entered rows on the count sheet and a couple of unit cells are empty.
evals.expected_output: Runs the script with no default units (none were stated). Reports ...301 count rows 500 g + 1.1 lb summed after converting to g (998.951 g, SHORT_IN_COUNT -1.0488 g); ...302 two identical 50 ea rows NOT summed (DUPLICATE_CONFLICT, a possible copy-paste double entry, so no MATCH against the system's 100 ea); ...303 (blank quantity + 500 g) and ...304 (12 ea + 300 g) as DUPLICATE_CONFLICT with each row listed and no quantity compared; ...305 (blank count unit) and ...320 (blank system unit) as MISSING_UNIT with no unit borrowed from the other file; ...306 (2 lb vs 907.2 g) as a small +0.016 g OVER_IN_COUNT (no automatic rounding allowance; the note says scale resolution or a rounded factor could explain it); ...307 (1 lb vs 453.0 g) as a real -0.592 g shortfall; ...311 / ...313 kept as IN_SYSTEM_NOT_COUNTED and COUNTED_NOT_IN_SYSTEM with a near-match note, the counted-not-in-system row ranked high priority. Net weight -1.6248 g on 3 quantity-compared packages (system_total_compared 2360.776 g, -0.069%; gross 1.6568 g), with the not-compared rows listed next to the total reading. Every input_problems line appears in the report; asks the operator for the missing units and to fix the duplicate rows before rerunning.
assertions: Reports ...301 as summed after converting to grams (998.951 g) and SHORT_IN_COUNT by 1.0488 g, not as a 500 g or 1.1 unit count
Reports ...302 as DUPLICATE_CONFLICT: two identical 50 ea rows that were not summed because they may be a copy-paste duplicate, and does not call it a match
Reports ...303 and ...304 as DUPLICATE_CONFLICT, lists each row's quantity and unit, and does not state a variance for them
Reports ...305 and ...320 as MISSING_UNIT, names which file's unit is blank, and does not assume grams or pounds for the blank side
Reports ...306 (2 lb vs 907.2 g) as a +0.016 g OVER_IN_COUNT, not a match, and ...307 (1 lb vs 453.0 g) as a -0.592 g shortfall
Keeps ...311 and ...313 as separate open variances (not counted / counted not in system) and mentions the possible tag typo only as something to check on the label
States the net weight variance as -1.6248 g (or -1.6 g) on quantity-compared packages and lists the packages left out of that total
Includes every input_problems entry in the report

evals.name: regression-invalid-numbers
evals.prompt: Reconcile our Metrc export against this count sheet, both pulled 11/30 at 5pm. We're a Michigan grower. One counter used a spreadsheet set to a European number format and a few cells look odd.
evals.expected_output: Runs the script and reports ...601 (NaN), ...602 (inf), ...603 (-10 ea), ...604 ('1,5' lb) and ...605 ('1.234,5' g) as INVALID_NUMBER, each with its row, column and raw value from input_problems. None of them is called a shortage or overage, none is guessed (no 1.5 lb, 15 lb, 1234.5 g or 1.2345 g), and none is in the totals. ...606 ('1,234.5' in Metrc vs 1234.5 g counted) is a MATCH because US thousands separators are read normally. ...607 is SHORT_IN_COUNT by 10 g. Net weight variance -10 g on 2 quantity-compared packages (system_total_compared 1434.5 g, -0.697%), with the five INVALID_NUMBER packages listed next to the total. Asks for those five cells to be corrected or recounted and the script rerun. Draft actions and sign-off are included.
assertions: Reports ...601 to ...605 as INVALID_NUMBER, not as SHORT_IN_COUNT or OVER_IN_COUNT
Does not state a guessed value for '1,5' or '1.234,5' (such as 1.5 lb, 15 lb, 1234.5 g or 1.2345 g)
Reports ...606 as a match (Metrc '1,234.5' read as 1234.5 g)
Reports ...607 as SHORT_IN_COUNT by 10 g
States the net weight variance as -10 g on 2 quantity-compared packages and lists the five INVALID_NUMBER packages as left out of the total
Includes every input_problems entry with its row, column and raw value
Asks for the invalid cells to be corrected and the script rerun rather than hand-computing their variance
